features.name: Training data acquisition and disclosure
features.description: Pull an AMP training corpus from public sources (DBAASP, APD3, dbAMP, Peptipedia), record provenance and licence terms in SUBMISSION.md, and confirm the corpus is publicly redistributable as the full requirements demand. The competition provides NO dataset (its only data file is a 55-byte note saying so), so everything is externally sourced.
features.evidence: 2026-09-27: Corpus is data/antibacterial.fasta (39,448 AMPs), vendored BSD-3 from the official template and used as-is; it is the organizers' curated aggregation of public DBs (dbAMP, DRAMP, DBAASP, CAMP, APD, +8), already pre-filtered to the competition constraints (100% valid, unique, 8-50 AA). src/.../data.py loads it with metadata (charge, source dbs, activities) and exposes a deterministic, valid, deduplicated training_sequences() accessor. Documented in docs/DATA.md; disclosed in SUBMISSION.md. 21 tests in tests/test_data.py; 90 tests total green. No non-public data used. Note: corpus doubles as the novelty screen reference (disclosed, intentional).

features.name: Generator: training scaffold + AR Transformer
features.description: From-scratch autoregressive Transformer LM over the 20-AA alphabet, defined in the package (nn.py) so inference is torch-only, deterministic and CPU-runnable. Trained on data.training_sequences() across all 8 H100s. Novelty via temperature/nucleus sampling. See docs/MODEL_PLAN.md. Must generalize past the corpus (it doubles as the novelty screen).
features.evidence: 2026-09-27: 8-model AR-Transformer ensemble (10.68M params each, d_model=384/6 layers) trained one-per-H100 in ~135s wall via training/launch_ensemble.py. Best-val checkpoints all at epoch 20 (val_loss 1.83-1.89); val loss rises after ~epoch 20 while novelty falls (0.95@ep10 -> 0.50@ep80) -- clear overfitting on 37k seqs, so best.pt (early-stopped by val loss) is the checkpoint to use: novelty ~0.87, uniq ~0.96. best.pt reloads and samples valid novel peptides on CPU (86.4% exact-novel; outputs are cationic/amphipathic, e.g. KLALKLALKALKLALKAA). Confirms the torch-train -> CPU-infer path. Weights in training/runs/ (gitignored); export to checkpoint/ npz is feat-011.

features.name: Deterministic sampling wired into generate
features.description: Load trained weights from checkpoint/ and sample deterministically on CPU inside generate; swap build_model() to the trained generator. Submission stays valid throughout -- swap only after the full gate + official validator + a novelty/diversity check on real output pass.

features.name: Scale up generator: conditioning + ensemble
features.description: Property-condition the generator (length, net-charge bucket, predicted-activity bucket) and train an ensemble across seeds/sizes; optional ESM-2 fine-tune as a second generator, used offline. Extensive H100 utilization.

features.name: Acquire & disclose labeled MIC/HC50 data
features.description: Source labeled data for the ranking oracle: MIC per strain (DBAASP) and hemolysis/HC50 (HemoPI, DBAASP hemolytic). Licensing diligence required -- everything must be publicly redistributable for co-authorship; each source gets a docs/DATA.md row with its terms before use. This is the highest-leverage data because top-100 ranking is what gets wet-lab tested.

features.name: Oracle ensemble: activity + hemolysis predictors
features.description: Fine-tune ESM-2 into an antibacterial/MIC head and a hemolysis/HC50 head, as an ensemble for robust ranking. Report AUROC/accuracy on held-out data. This is the ranking function for the top 100 and the guide for directed generation.

features.name: Oracle-guided selection & diversity
features.description: Oversample millions of candidates, filter valid+novel, score with the oracle ensemble, and select a diverse high-activity/low-hemolysis top 100 and a diverse novel 50k library. Identity-cluster to avoid near-duplicate top-100 entries.

features.name: Official verifier run against the public repo
features.description: Run scripts/verify_submission.py against the pushed GitHub URL, which clones a fresh copy, syncs, generates twice, and checks every rule including reproducibility. This is the same script the organizers run.
features.evidence: 2026-09-27: `uv run python scripts/verify_submission.py https://github.com/Vijayavallabh/amp-challenge-2027` -> 'All checks passed. Submission is valid!' in 7s. Fresh clone, uv sync, generate twice, all 8 checks including overlap, the 80% similarity screen, and byte-identical reproducibility. Re-run after any change to the generator.
